2608.14399.title: Whose doctor does the AI recommend? An algorithm audit of reputation and demographic signals in large language model-assisted physician choice
2608.14399.paper_summary: Patients increasingly ask large language model (LLM) assistants which doctor to see, making these systems AI infomediaries: algorithms that intermediate one person's choice among other people and thereby decide, silently and at scale, which physicians become visible. We report a prespecified randomized algorithm audit of what causally moves those recommendations. Seven models (six open-weight; gpt-4o-mini) each chose among five synthetic family-medicine physician cards whose attributes were independently randomized across 3,024 choice sets, three patient personas, nine prompt paraphrases and nine experimental arms, yielding 40,068 scored responses; gender and ethnicity were signaled through names following correspondence-audit methodology. Reputation signals dominate: raising a rating from 3.9 to 4.7 increases choice probability by 31.4 percentage points (pp), and raising the fee from $90 to $190 lowers it by 20.0 pp. Demographic parity is rejected, but not in the direction human audit studies predict: female-signaled names gain 2.5 pp, and Hispanic-, South-Asian- and Black-signaled names gain 1.3-2.9 pp over White-signaled names, tilts worth $7-$14 per visit in fee-equivalent terms, and a content-free first-listed position is worth $11. Yet models mentioned gender or ethnicity in at most 0.03% of their stated reasons and abstained in 0.39% of trials, so these effects are invisible in the models' own explanations, and transparency obligations relying on model self-report would not detect them. One reasoning model failed the prespecified auditability gate outright. The frozen design makes the audit repeatable: any new model can be assessed against identical stimuli, making recurring behavioural audit, rather than self-reported explanation, the monitoring technology fit for purpose.
2608.14399.paper_summary_zh: 病人越來越多地詢問大型語言模型（LLM）助手應該看哪位醫生，使這些系統成為人工智慧資訊中介：算法在不同人之間進行選擇，並因此靜默且大規模地決定哪些醫生變得可見。我們報告了一項預先指定的隨機算法審計，旨在探討那些推薦的因果因素。七個模型（六個開放權重；gpt-4o-mini）各自從五個合成家庭醫學醫生卡片中選擇，這些卡片的屬性在3,024個選擇集、三個病人角色、九個提示改寫和九個實驗組之間獨立隨機化，產生了40,068個得分回應；性別和種族通過名字進行標示，遵循對應審計方法論。聲譽信號主導：將評分從3.9提高到4.7會使選擇概率增加31.4個百分點（pp），而將費用從90美元提高到190美元則會使其降低20.0 pp。人口統計平等被拒絕，但並非朝著人類審計研究預測的方向：女性標示的名字獲得2.5 pp，而西班牙裔、南亞裔和黑人標示的名字則比白人標示的名字獲得1.3-2.9 pp，這在費用等值的條件下相當於每次就診7-14美元的價值，且沒有內容的首位位置價值為11美元。然而，模型在其陳述理由中提到性別或種族的比例最多僅為0.03%，並在0.39%的試驗中保持沉默，因此這些影響在模型自身的解釋中是不可見的，依賴模型自我報告的透明度義務無法檢測到它們。一個推理模型徹底未通過預先指定的可審計性門檻。凍結的設計使得審計可重複：任何新模型都可以根據相同的刺激進行評估，使得重複的行為審計，而不是自我報告的解釋，成為適合目的的監測技術。
